name: Handbook
title: Handbook: how the starter site is built and checked
description: How the starter is put together: each page type, what it is for, where it sits in the address scheme, and the checks it must pass.
intro: The kit builds a small set of page types, and every page on a site is one of them. Knowing the type tells you its address, its layout and the rules it is held to.
This section holds one of each, written about the kit itself so that no niche is implied. A real project keeps the structure and replaces the words.

blocks.p: Every address is lowercase, ends with a slash and is at most three levels deep. Breadcrumbs mirror it, so a reader always sees where they are.

The research decides each address once. A content file with no matching row in the keyword map fails the build, and so does a worked example or guide whose parent is missing, because it would have no way in.

Each type has a minimum amount of text before the AdSense review will pass it: 300 words for hubs and the home page, 600 for tools, 800 for guides, and 200 for trust pages. These are floors to reach with useful detail. Padding a page to reach one is against the kit's own rules.
